raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through for my fields this year.

---

*(thinking in my own voice)*

I'm getting on now — 45 years old, been working these fields since I married into this village. My man works some days at the town, but with seven mouths at home, this land is what keeps us going. I only finished primary school, so I don't do all that calculating like the younger ones from the agriculture college. I watch my fields, I listen to my neighbors, and I mostly do what I did last year unless something went wrong.

I have 10.1 mu total. Like most of us in the village, I split it: the good flat piece, about 7 mu, I do wheat then maize — one after the other, same as always. The other 3.1 mu on the edge, I plant cotton. Cotton is how we get cash in hand before the New Year. Grain is for the family mostly, and a bit to sell.

**Wheat** — I already put it in back in October. Seed I bought from the co-op, not saved — the saved seed last time gave weak stand. I put down about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu when I planted (that's around 15 kg urea worth of nitrogen, the shopkeeper helps me figure it). Now it's spring, the wheat is greening up. In a couple weeks when it's jointing I'll topdress another scoop of urea per mu — maybe 8-10 kg — and run the well water once then. I'll irrigate again at heading if no rain comes. Three times water at most — pumping is expensive, my husband complains about the electric bill. Last year I got about 420 kg/mu, neighbor Wang's wife got 460 but she uses more fertilizer than me. I can't afford her way every year.

**Maize** — Right after wheat harvest in June, same field, I plant maize. Very tight, maybe four days between combining wheat and planting maize. I use hybrid seed, the "Zhengdan" kind the village agent recommends — everyone plants it, so I do too. I don't till much, just direct seed into the stubble, that's what we all do now. I put fertilizer in at planting, about one bag compound per mu again, then topdress urea when it's knee-high, maybe 10 kg. If July is dry I irrigate once or twice. Maize is less work than wheat honestly. Last year I got around 450 kg/mu.

**Cotton** — This is the headache crop but it pays. I plant mid-April on the 3.1 mu corner plot. I buy Bt cotton seed, the kind for bollworm resistance — without it the pests eat you alive. I put base fertilizer before planting, about 15 kg compound, and topdress again at flowering with urea and some potash. Cotton drinks water, but I only irrigate twice because of the cost. Pesticide I spray maybe 4-5 times through the summer for bollworm, aphids, whiteflies — this is where most of the cotton money goes. Picking starts late September, and it runs into October, three or four pickings. My mother-in-law and my two older daughters help pick — without the family we couldn't do cotton, hiring pickers would eat all the profit. Last year I got about 240 kg of lint per mu.

I'm not going to change much this year. Fertilizer prices went up a little but cotton price looked okay at market last fall, so I'll keep the same plan. If summer looks dry, I'll skip one maize irrigation to save the electric for cotton — cotton needs the water more at flowering.
